text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation's subsidiary realises 99.5 billion naira from sale of oil products in 1995.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha congratulates U.S. president Bill Clinton on his re-election and expresses his belief U.S.-Nigerian ties will grow stronger.
- Truck explodes because of faulty disc at Warri oil depot in the midwest causing pandemonium, witnesses say.
- Umbrella association of chambers of commerce and industry urges the military government to introduce cautious reflationary measures in next year's budget to stimulate economic growth.
- National Electric Power Authority slashes costs of electricity metres by 70 percent, official says.
- Banks withdraw interest on current accounts because of current lull in borrowing, bankers say.

- Nigerian stock exchange cancels controversial purchase of 1.8 million shares of American International Insurance Company by General Insurance Company Ltd; says shares should be offered on the floor of the exchange.
- Asians stay away from Lagos trade fair as European companies from France, Germany and Poland take centre stage.
